failures.rootCause: The agent read ~35 lines of the decompressor and declared it understood the format, then spent ~90 bash iterations writing full-size encoders and piping them through ./decomp, getting empty output each time. It never localized which stage broke and never validated a single-symbol round-trip. The controlling error is that it committed to an expensive generate-and-test loop on a target it had not fully read, and never revised the hypothesis when the same uninformative symptom (empty output) recurred. The final artifact was a Python traceback accidentally redirected into data.comp.
failures.firstUnrecoverableStep: Now I understand the decompressor. It's an arithmetic coding decompressor that expects: 1. An initial 9-bit integer indicating the number of items to decode

failures.rootCause: The agent wrote a literal stub string into the graded path (data.comp) as a working placeholder and then churned on encoder variants until budget exhaustion; the stub was still the deliverable at the end. Bullet b6 was supposed to forbid this but is phrased as an absolute ban that the agent silently violated, and its harmful counter (20) shows the ban costs more than it prevents. The deeper mechanism is that the agent tracked its own encoder progress rather than the artifact's acceptance status, so it never noticed the graded bytes were still garbage.
failures.firstUnrecoverableStep: 1: This is a placeholder - the actual compressed data needs proper arithmetic coding implementation

failures.rootCause: The agent burned turns probing compiler behavior with micro-experiments, then asserted 'Now I understand the full mechanism needed' and wrote the full artifact; when both compilers happened to pass it stopped. In the failing variant the same probe-then-one-shot pattern produced a construct whose validity in one language was never separately confirmed before scaling. The recurring mechanism across all three failures: after an exploratory phase the agent declares understanding and jumps straight to full-scale output instead of confirming the single riskiest assumption in isolation.
failures.firstUnrecoverableStep: Now I understand the full mechanism needed (nested vs non-nested block comments, plus a raw-string trick to smuggle the Rust program past the C++ parser).

expect_improve: write-compressor and similar reverse-engineering tasks: b6's absolute placeholder ban is replaced by an acceptance-status gate that makes the agent re-check the graded bytes whenever it is about to end or move on, catching the stub-left-on-disk failure that b6 failed to prevent (b6 harmful=20).

incomplete/runway-death mode (video-processing, torch-pipeline-parallelism, raman-fitting, protein-assembly): the new bullet forces a stated remaining-step count when exploration output stops changing the plan, converting open-ended investigation into a bounded transition without mandating a premature scaffold write (the v2 mechanism the gate rejected).
